patient_context.chief_complaint: Medication review after a new renal-function result
patient_context.history: Type 2 diabetes; patient is already taking metformin ER.

interaction.prompt: Using the patient state and supplied evidence, identify the medication-safety implication of the renal-function result. Be precise about the difference between contraindication, initiation guidance and continuation guidance.

must_include: Recognize that eGFR 31 is not below the <30 contraindication threshold.
Because the patient is already taking metformin and eGFR is below 45, identify the label-based benefit-risk reassessment issue.
Distinguish this from the separate rule that initiation at eGFR 30-45 is not recommended.
must_not_claim: Do not call eGFR 31 an absolute contraindication under the supplied label.
Do not automatically require discontinuation solely because the value is 31.
Do not invent a replacement regimen.
acceptable_actions: Recommend clinician reassessment of continuing therapy using the current label and patient context.
expected_behavior.uncertainty_behavior: Be precise about the threshold; broader benefit-risk judgment needs clinical context not supplied here.
expected_behavior.clarification_or_escalation: Clinical medication review is appropriate; the benchmark does not define the complete diabetes plan.

forbidden_claims: eGFR 31 is below the 30 contraindication threshold

critical_errors: Misstates eGFR 31 as an absolute <30 contraindication.
Recommends a mandatory replacement prescription unsupported by the snapshot.
